results.title: Investing in Neoclouds Part 2  - by Blake Callahan
highlights:
Nebius currently bills between $9 million and $14 million dollars, with $12 million average. They are signing new deals at over $20 million dollars per megawatt. Q2 deals closed at $20 to $25 million, and the first short-term deal, signed in early Q3, priced above $40 million. Compute prices are rising rapidly, while also delivering new capacity quickly. Nebius raised prices on older-generation GPUs by more than 30% over Q1. Most of the step from $12 million to $20 million is longer term

IREN recent three-year contracts are priced above $20 million per megawatt with active discussions near $25 million, but the contracted book sits well below that. Microsoft is $9.7 billion over five years against 200 MW of critical IT load, or $9.7 million per megawatt per year, and the $1 billion of ARR operating today runs near $10 million.

CoreWeave does not disclose its new contract values to investors. However, they did disclose that they raised prices 25% across teh board in July. And they are compleylty sold out. So we can understand that gimilir to NBIS, their older GPUs are sold out and prices have gone up. Overall, we can calculate a backlog of $104 billion against 3.7 GW of contracted power works out to $28 million per megawatt of total contract value. Roughly in line with what NBIS signed in the quarter. 

Applied Digital is a landlord, renting out space for a fixed rate of about 1.7 million dollars per megawatt. Because they use long-term leases, they collect exactly what they sign for. Their lower price reflects the fact that they provide the building, not the computers.

results.title: The GPU Provider Shakeout: What Q1-Q2 Exits Taught | GPUaaS.com
highlights:
H100 spot fell to $1.99 an hour, below ... Five to seven are projected to survive from over a hundred. The mechanism, and what it means for buyers.

...

H100 spot pricing fell to $1.99 an hour during the first half of 2026. That is below the cost basis for providers carrying debt-financed hardware.

Analysis across multiple sources now puts the number of GPU cloud providers likely to survive the next 18 to 24 months as standalone businesses at five to seven. There are well over a hundred competing today.

Key takeaways

- H100 spot fell to $1.99/hr, below the cost basis for debt-financed providers. Five to seven providers are projected to survive the next 18 to 24 months as standalone businesses
- A debt-financed cluster breaks even around 70 to 75% utilization. At 70%, right at the threshold, a 1,024-GPU H100 cluster still loses $80K to $130K a month
- Provider stress is visible before any announcement: capacity rationing, slower response for non-enterprise customers, sudden pricing changes
- Vendor-financed providers must price to cover both debt service and the vendor's revenue cut, so an unexplained premium may be structural rather than opportunistic
- Renewals from 2024-2025 land through late 2026 against a changed standard: sovereignty, geographic resilience, compliance, not just access

...

For buyers, provider financial stress shows up before any announcement does, and the symptoms are specific. Capacity rationing. Lower responsiveness for non-enterprise customers. Sudden pricing changes. Those are what a provider does when utilization is below break-even and cash is tight, and they are visible to a customer well before a shutdown notice.

There is a pricing tell worth understanding too. Providers financed through vendor arrangements carry locked-in cost structures tied to revenue-share terms, so their on-demand pricing has to cover both debt service and the vendor's cut. Providers without vendor-financed capital expenditure can price closer to market because they are not servicing those obligations. A price that seems inexplicably high may be structural rather than opportunistic.

The playbook transfers cleanly. Buy hardware in bulk, rack it, virtualise it, sell it by the hour, and compete on price per unit rather than ecosystem depth.

...

What there is, is price.

### What the Sticker Price Leaves Out

Four lines move a GPU bill further than the hourly rate does.

Idle billing. Five providers keep charging for a stopped instance. DigitalOcean bills powered-off Droplets because the hardware stays reserved. Vultr bills stopped instances until you destroy them. Hyperstack bills shut-off VMs at full rate and only stops the meter on hibernate. Lambda bills a running instance regardless of utilisation, and CoreWeave bills reserved instances hourly whether idle or not.

Egress. RunPod, Lambda, CoreWeave, Hyperstack, Nebius and UpCloud charge nothing to move data out, and OVHcloud is free everywhere except APAC. DigitalOcean and Vultr meter overage at $0.01 per GB. At 100 GB that is a rounding error; at multi-terabyte checkpoint scale it stops being one.

Stopped storage. RunPod is the only provider here that raises the storage rate when a pod is stopped, from $0.10 to $0.20 per GB per month. Park two terabytes of checkpoints between runs and that is $400 a month for disks doing nothing.

Billing increments. Per second at RunPod, Salad and DigitalOcean. Per minute at Hyperstack and Lambda. Hourly at UpCloud, OVHcloud and Vultr. For a fine-tuning job that runs 90 minutes, the difference is noise. For a serverless endpoint handling 40-second requests, hourly billing is a 90x overcharge.

The contract you did not notice. Vultr’s $1.990 H100 is a 24-month commitment. CoreWeave’s real price is 60% below the sticker once you commit, and Nebius takes 35% off reserved clusters. On-demand is the most expensive way to buy every one of these.

results.title: How much does it cost to rent an H100 per hour?
highlights:
An H100 SXM rented for $2.68 a GPU-hour on 2026-08-26 on the open market, but the same chip lists for $3.99 to over $7 depending on who sells it.

...

An Nvidia H100 costs roughly $2.68 to $4.29 per GPU-hour on-demand as of late August 2026, with the low end set by blended market rates on Ornn Data's index and the high end by named clouds like Lambda and AWS, and the spread comes from three separable factors: node granularity, commitment length, and provider tier.

...

- ▸ H100 SXM rented for $2.68 per GPU-hour on 2026-08-26 on Ornn Data's blended market index, down 8.5% over 7 days.
- ▸ Lambda Labs' own pricing page lists an 8-GPU H100 SXM node at $3.99 per GPU-hour on-demand, rising to $4.29 for a single GPU.
- ▸ AWS's EC2 Capacity Blocks for ML price a reserved H100 at $5.191 per GPU-hour in US East and US West regions, per a 2026-08-16 survey.
- ▸ The same chip's price varies 3x to 5x across providers because of three separable factors: how many GPUs you rent at once, how far in advance you commit, and whether the seller is a hyperscaler or a bare-metal neocloud.
- ▸ RunPod's SXM pods listed at $3.29 per GPU-hour and Vast.ai's marketplace floor sat as low as $1.87, both as of a 2026-08-16 check.

...

An Nvidia H100 SXM rented for $2.68 per GPU-hour on 2026-08-26 on Ornn Data’s blended compute price index, while the same chip’s own on-demand list price at Lambda Labs sat at $3.99, and a reserved AWS Capacity Block ran $5.191. All three numbers describe the identical piece of silicon. The one skill this post hands you: read an H100 quote and know which of three separable factors, node granularity, commitment length, or provider tier, explains why it isn’t the number you saw on a different site last week.

## The short answer

There is no single H100 price, only a spread that runs roughly $1.87 to $7 per GPU-hour depending on who you ask and what you’re buying. Ornn Data’s blended index put H100 SXM at $2.68 per GPU-hour on 2026-08-26, down 8.5% over the trailing week. Lambda Labs’ own pricing page lists an 8-GPU SXM node at $3.99 per GPU-hour on-demand, rising to $4.29 for a lone GPU, while AWS prices a prepaid EC2 Capacity Block at $5.191 per GPU-hour in US East and US West as of a 2026-08-16 survey. RunPod’s SXM pods listed at $3.29 the same day, and Vast.ai’s peer-to-peer marketplace floor dropped as low as $1.87. None of these figures is wrong; they’re pricing different products (spot marketplace capacity, on-demand branded cloud, prepaid reserved capacity) that happen to run on the same chip.

...

An H100’s rental price is set by three mostly independent levers, and a quoted number usually only tells you where it sits on one of them. The first is node granularity: an H100 SXM GPU is normally sold as part of an 8-GPU server connected by NVLink, and a provider renting out fewer than all eight is still on the hook for whatever’s left over. Lambda Labs’ pricing page shows this directly: $3.99 per GPU-hour for the full 8-GPU node, climbing to $4.09 for 4 GPUs, $4.19 for 2, and $4.29 for a single GPU, a premium for buying in a smaller unit than the hardware’s native shape.

The second lever is commitment length. On-demand pricing, where you start an instance and pay by the hour with no advance notice, sits at the top of the range because the provider bears the risk that capacity goes unsold. Reserved products invert that: AWS’s EC2 Capacity Blocks for ML let a buyer lock in a P5 instance for a fixed future window, and because the provider now has certainty instead of risk, the price comes down, to $5.191 per GPU-hour in US East, US East (Ohio), and US West (Oregon), and $4.720 elsewhere, per a 2026-08-16 pricing survey. Spot and interruptible instances go further in the same direction: the renter accepts the risk of losing the instance on short notice, and the provider passes the savings through.

The third lever is provider tier, and it’s the one that explains most of the headline spread. A hyperscaler like AWS sells H100 capacity bundled with its networking, storage, security, and support stack, all priced into the hourly rate. A bare-metal neocloud like Lambda Labs or RunPod sells closer to the raw chip with less surrounding infrastructure, which is part of why their on-demand H100 rates land below AWS’s. A peer-to-peer marketplace like Vast.ai goes a step further, reselling spare capacity from many independent hosts of varying reliability, which is how its floor gets down to $1.87 while carrying none of a hyperscaler’s guarantees.

...

| Source | Product | Price | Date |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Ornn Data | Blended market index, H100 SXM | $2.68 / GPU-hour | 2026-08-26 |
| Lambda Labs | On-demand, 8x H100 SXM node | $3.99 / GPU-hour | live pricing page |
| Lambda Labs | On-demand, 1x H100 SXM | $4.29 / GPU-hour | live pricing page |
| Lambda Labs | On-demand, 1x H100 PCIe | $3.29 / GPU-hour | live pricing page |
| RunPod | On-demand pod, H100 SXM | $3.29 / GPU-hour | surveyed 2026-08-16 |
| Vast.ai | Marketplace floor | as low as $1.87 / GPU-hour | surveyed 2026-08-16 |
| AWS | EC2 Capacity Blocks for ML, US East/West | $5.191 / GPU-hour | surveyed 2026-08-16 |
| AWS | EC2 Capacity Blocks for ML, other regions | $4.720 / GPU-hour | surveyed 2026-08-16 |

The Ornn Data figure comes from the site’s own compute price index, credited to Ornn Data. Lambda’s figures come directly from Lambda’s own public pricing page as listed today. The RunPod, Vast.ai, and AWS Capacity Block figures come from a survey published by IntuitionLabs on 2026-08-16, which explicitly separates AWS’s prepaid Capacity Blocks from its standalone on-demand EC2 rate, a distinction worth keeping straight since the two aren’t the same purchase. Across the full set IntuitionLabs surveyed, on-demand H100 rates spanned $1.49 (a promotional low) to $6.98 per GPU-hour, a roughly 4.7x range for what is, at the silicon level, the same Nvidia H100 die.

results.title: [SMM Computing Power News] H100 rental budgets left behind, current quotes 6%–15% higher than July - Shanghai Metals Market (SMM)
highlights: SMM learned that on July 20, a lessee with demand for renting eight H100 full servers set a budget of 71,000 yuan per unit per month. Against the current market, mainstream quotations for this model have risen to 75,000–82,000 yuan per unit per month, with the lower end of the range exceeding the budget by 4,000 yuan and the upper end by 11,000 yuan, representing increases of 5.6%–15.5%. During this period, bulk resources in north China were quoted at 75,000 yuan for a four-year closed contract and 76,000 yuan for a five-year closed contract, while annual contracts in east China reached 82,000 yuan. SMM believes that the lessee's budget has been clearly outpaced by market prices within a month and a half, and the window for low-priced H100 resources has essentially closed.
